validity.recommendation: Rewrite as the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail line (about 820 mm or two 800 mm strings, 1975) and drop the Rozdilna stop, or merge with that line; keep P0787 separate.
validity.researcher_notes: The row mixes facts from different lines. Its name joins the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail line with Rozdilna, which belongs to P0787. The 1200 mm diameter matches P0786. The 24 bcm figure is a three-string system number. The 164 km length is far below the route. Ukrainian Wikipedia says the Shebelinka-Izmail line started in 1975 with two 800 mm strings. Moldovatransgaz lists it with 820 mm and 7.3 bcm per year. The line is real, but this row's numbers do not describe it.

fills.researcher_notes: Ukrainian Wikipedia's article on the Shebelinka-Izmail corridor treats the lines in it as gas transmission. It names the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail line but not the extra Rozdilna stop in this row's name.
No source dated 2024 or later names this line. The row's identity is unclear (see validity note), so no status ref was attached.
Ukrainian Wikipedia says the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail line was commissioned in 1975 with two 800 mm strings. I did not fill it because this row's identity is unclear.

The only known source for 24 bcm per year is a 2012 table that lumps the Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail line with three Shebelinka-Izmail strings. That is a system figure. Moldovatransgaz gives 7.3 bcm per year for the Shebelinka line in Moldova. No segment source supports 24.

No source states 164 km for this named route. The sheet's own cited page is about the Shebelinka gas field. The named route runs from Kharkiv Oblast to Izmail, far longer than 164 km. Moldovatransgaz gives 91.817 km for the Moldovan part alone.

Moldovatransgaz gives 820 mm for the Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail line, and Ukrainian Wikipedia says two 800 mm strings. 1200 mm matches the Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail line (P0786), not this one. Not supported.
Ukrainian Wikipedia's corridor article names the line from Shebelinka via Dnipropetrovsk and Kryvyi Rih to Izmail. The end points match. The article does not use the Rozdilna stop in this row's name.
